category: certificates, declarations and other one-per-asset documents
title: Fill 200 certificates of conformity from one asset list
why: Every asset needs its own certificate, and each one is the same document with a different tag, serial number and date. Typing them one at a time takes days and invites copying mistakes.
idea: Keep the assets in a spreadsheet and write the certificate once in Word, with a marker wherever a detail changes. The computer then makes a separate, correctly named Word file for every row. A correction is made once and the whole set is remade in seconds.
try_label: Try the working version with made-up files
how: The asset list sits in Excel: one row per asset, one column per detail, with a name at the top of each column.
The certificate is written once in Word. Where a detail changes, the column name goes in double curly brackets.
The computer reads the list row by row and fills a copy of the certificate for each asset, numbering them as it goes.
Rows with a missing detail or a failed inspection are held back and listed with the reason, instead of producing a wrong certificate.
need: The asset list as an Excel sheet, with tidy column names and no merged cells
Your approved certificate wording as a Word file
Someone authorised to check and sign the finished set
before:
AHU-006 | Air handling unit | SN674351 | 05-09-2026
P-018 | Circulation pump | (no serial) | 11-09-2026
FD-001 | Fire door set | SN150631 | 05-10-2026
after:
CoC_AHU-006.docx  (certificate CoC-2026-0001)
CoC_FD-001.docx   (certificate CoC-2026-0002)
Held back: P-018, missing serial number
person: A certificate of conformity is a formal declaration, so a person checks the set and signs. The signature line is left empty on purpose: the computer fills in details, it does not approve anything.
watch_out: A column name spelled differently in the list and in the template leaves a blank on every certificate.
Dates print the way they are shown in Excel, so format the column before you start.
A large logo inside the template is copied into every file and makes the whole set heavy.
explain: We write the certificate once and let the asset list fill in the rest, so 200 certificates take seconds instead of days and nobody retypes a serial number.
credit: This one has been built and tested on a made-up list of 200 assets.
